questions.question: In `[Route("api/[controller]")] public class StudentsController : ControllerBase`, what route does this serve?
options: api/StudentsController
api/students
controller/students
It needs an explicit route, this won't compile
questions.explanation: [controller] is replaced with the class name minus the 'Controller' suffix, lowercased by convention in the resulting route — StudentsController serves api/students.

questions.question: What's the equivalent of Minimal API's `Results.Ok(value)` inside an MVC controller action?
options: `return value;`
`return Ok(value);` — inherited from ControllerBase
`Results.Ok(value)` — same syntax, no change
`return Results.Value(value);`
questions.explanation: ControllerBase provides Ok(), NotFound(), Created(), etc. as inherited instance methods (Module 2's inheritance) — same concept as Results.*, different calling style.

questions.question: What does `builder.Services.AddSingleton<IStudentRepository, InMemoryStudentRepository>();` do?
options: Creates an instance immediately and prints it
Registers IStudentRepository with the DI container — one shared instance of InMemoryStudentRepository will be handed out for the app's entire lifetime whenever IStudentRepository is requested
Makes InMemoryStudentRepository the only class allowed in the project
Nothing — this line has no effect without further configuration
questions.explanation: This registers the mapping in the DI container: 'when something needs an IStudentRepository, give it this SHARED InMemoryStudentRepository instance.' Singleton means one instance for the whole app's lifetime.

questions.question: Why does `StudentsController` take `IStudentRepository` (not `InMemoryStudentRepository`) in its constructor?
options: No real reason, either would work identically

Dependency Inversion (Module 2) — the controller depends on the abstraction, so the concrete implementation can be swapped (e.g., for a database-backed one in Module 6) without changing the controller
Interfaces are required syntax for all constructor parameters
InMemoryStudentRepository doesn't have a public constructor
questions.explanation: This is DIP applied directly: the controller only knows about the CAPABILITY (IStudentRepository), not the specific implementation — exactly the OrderProcessor/INotifier pattern from Module 2, lesson 08.

questions.question: Which lifetime is appropriate for a service that must hold ONE consistent piece of state shared across the entire running application (like an in-memory list acting as a fake database)?
options: Transient
Scoped
Singleton
None of these support shared state
questions.explanation: Singleton creates exactly one instance for the whole app's lifetime — perfect for a shared in-memory store where every request should see the same underlying data.

questions.question: Minimal API handlers can also receive DI-registered services, as extra parameters, the same way controllers receive them via their constructor.
questions.explanation: `app.MapGet("/students", (IStudentRepository repository) => repository.GetAll());` — the DI container resolves `repository` automatically, just like it resolves controller constructor parameters.
